scenario: Eight relay runners — Fontaine, Greer, Holt, Ishida, Joyal, Kwan, Lester, and Mori — are assigned to exactly one of three relay teams: the Cranes, the Falcons, and the Hawks. The Cranes have three runners, the Falcons have three runners, and the Hawks have two runners. The following conditions apply:

rules.description: Fontaine and Greer are not on the same team.
Holt and Ishida are on the same team.
If Joyal is on the Cranes, then Kwan is on the Falcons.
If Lester is on the Hawks, then Fontaine is on the Cranes.
Mori is not on the Falcons.
Exactly one of Greer, Joyal, and Kwan is on the Cranes.

With Joyal also on the Falcons, neither Joyal nor (if Kwan ends up elsewhere) can be that one Cranes member from the group — ultimately, placing both Fontaine and Joyal on the Falcons while satisfying the Lester-Hawks conditional and the exactly-one constraint simultaneously leads to a contradiction in every possible arrangement.

questions.questionStem: If Holt and Greer are on the same team, then which one of the following must be true?

explanations.correct: If Holt and Greer are on the same team, then since Holt and Ishida must also be on the same team (rule 2), all three of Greer, Holt, and Ishida must be on the same team. That team must have exactly three slots, so Greer, Holt, and Ishida fill an entire team. They cannot be on the Hawks (which has only two slots), so they are on the Cranes or the Falcons. Fontaine and Greer must be on different teams, so Fontaine is not on whichever team holds Greer, Holt, and Ishida. Mori cannot be on the Falcons (rule 5). Exactly one of {Greer, Joyal, Kwan} must be on the Cranes. Since Greer is on one of the three-person teams (Cranes or Falcons), if Greer is on the Cranes, that satisfies the exactly-one rule and Joyal and Kwan must not be on the Cranes. If Greer is on the Falcons, then exactly one of {Joyal, Kwan} must be on the Cranes. In all valid arrangements, Mori — unable to go to the Falcons — ends up on the Hawks in every scenario, because the two remaining non-Hawks spots (once Greer+Holt+Ishida fill one team) are claimed by Fontaine, Joyal/Kwan, and Lester in ways that always push Mori to the Hawks.
explanations.A: Fontaine could be on the Cranes or the Falcons, not necessarily the Hawks. When Greer+Holt+Ishida are on the Falcons, Fontaine can be on the Cranes.
explanations.B: Joyal could be on the Cranes or the Hawks depending on the arrangement. Not forced to the Falcons.
explanations.C: Kwan's placement depends on which team Greer occupies and how the exactly-one rule is satisfied. Kwan is not necessarily on the Cranes.
explanations.D: Lester can be on the Cranes, Falcons, or Hawks. No rule forces Lester specifically to the Cranes under this condition.
explanations.E: Correct. Mori cannot be on the Falcons (rule 5). With Greer, Holt, and Ishida filling one of the two three-runner teams, and Fontaine excluded from that team, the remaining runners for the other three-runner team and the Hawks create no room for Mori except the Hawks in every valid arrangement.

questions.questionStem: If Kwan is on the Hawks, then each of the following could be true EXCEPT:

explanations.correct: If Kwan is on the Hawks, then Mori cannot also be on the Hawks (Hawks holds only two runners, and Mori cannot be on the Falcons, so Mori must be on the Cranes). With Kwan on the Hawks, the second Hawks runner is not Mori — it must be someone else. Actually: Hawks has exactly 2 slots; Kwan occupies one. The other must come from {Fontaine, Greer, Holt, Ishida, Joyal, Lester, Mori}. Mori cannot be on the Falcons, so Mori is on the Cranes or Hawks. If Mori is not on the Hawks (since Kwan is there and the second slot is taken by someone else), Mori must be on the Cranes. The exactly-one rule: exactly one of {Greer, Joyal, Kwan} on the Cranes. Kwan=Hawks, so exactly one of {Greer, Joyal} must be on the Cranes. Fontaine≠Greer. If Greer=Falcons, then Joyal must be on the Cranes (to satisfy the exactly-one rule, since Greer is not on Cranes). Joyal=Cranes triggers the conditional: Kwan must be on Falcons. But Kwan is on the Hawks — CONTRADICTION. So Greer cannot be on the Falcons when Kwan is on the Hawks.
explanations.A: Fontaine can be on the Cranes. For example: Cranes — Fontaine, Joyal, Mori (with Joyal=Cranes triggering Kwan=Falcons, but Kwan=Hawks — contradiction). Actually Joyal=Cranes is forbidden here too. So Cranes must have Greer (from {Greer,Joyal}). Cranes: Greer + two others not including Joyal (who must be Falcons or Hawks). If Hawks: Kwan + Joyal, then exactly one of {Greer,Joyal}=Cranes: Joyal=Hawks, so Greer=Cranes ✓. Cranes: Greer+Fontaine+Mori or Greer+Holt+Ishida+... Fontaine=Cranes is possible if Cranes has Greer+Fontaine+Mori. Valid ✓.
explanations.B: Correct. If Greer is on the Falcons, then the exactly-one rule (with Kwan=Hawks) requires Joyal to be on the Cranes. But Joyal=Cranes fires the conditional, forcing Kwan=Falcons — contradicting Kwan=Hawks.
explanations.C: Holt can be on the Cranes. Since Holt+Ishida must be together, Ishida is also on the Cranes. Cranes: Holt+Ishida+Greer (with Greer satisfying the exactly-one rule). Hawks: Kwan+Mori. Falcons: Fontaine+Joyal+Lester. Fontaine≠Greer ✓; Mori not Falcons ✓; Joyal=Falcons (not Cranes) so conditional doesn't fire ✓. Valid ✓.
explanations.D: Joyal can be on the Falcons as long as Greer (not Joyal) is the one from {Greer,Joyal} satisfying the exactly-one rule on the Cranes. That is fully compatible with Kwan=Hawks.
explanations.E: Lester can be on the Cranes. For example: Cranes — Greer, Holt, Ishida (with Greer as the exactly-one member); actually Lester also needs to fit. Cranes: Greer+Lester+Mori; Hawks: Kwan+X; Falcons: remaining. Valid arrangements exist.
